To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## 1. How to treat the Seller's framing

Before the substance, three points about how the package is presented. None of them binds us.

- **"Settled at principal level", "FINAL", "not intended to be re-opened".** Nothing on our side supports this. Several Seller positions match our fallbacks: the 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and the 18-month period. Those fallbacks can only be offered with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given. Unless Amelia confirms otherwise in writing, we should treat this as the Seller's opening position, not an agreed bargain.
- **"[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note".** These are one party's labels. They ask us to skip scrutiny of almost every substantive clause. We have reviewed everything on its merits. We also do not accept the statement that "the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package". Our playbook rejects both.
- **"Market context".** The cited ranges (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge bars) are unsourced advocacy. They do not change our authorised positions.

**Recommendation:** say expressly in our cover note that we do not accept the "[STANDARD]/FINAL" characterisation, that no fallback has been authorised, and that every clause remains open to mark-up.

## 2. Issue-by-issue departures from the playbook

### A. Liability regime

| Item | Seller | Playbook | Push back |
|---|---|---|---|
| **12.1 General cap** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a fallback that needs Amelia's written authority (not given) | Hold at **AUD 6,000,000**. Do not concede 20%. Escalate to Amelia only if the team wants authority to use the fallback. |
| **12.2 De minimis** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. 5x our level. It would exclude many mid-sized SaaS claims. |
| **12.2 Basket** | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, **first dollar** once exceeded | Reject both the size (5x) and the deductible structure. Once tipped, the Seller is liable from the first dollar. |
| **12.3 General period** | 18 months | 24 months. 18 is a fallback needing Amelia's approval (not given) | Hold at **24 months**. |
| **12.3 / 13 "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | Blanket application | Categories kept separate. No hidden general-regime override | **Delete.** This sweeper pulls Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants into the general cap, basket and time limits by default. Replace it with an express statement that the general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. |

### B. Fundamental / Title warranties

The Seller wants capacity and title warranties to carry the same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity". This would cap title to the whole asset at 20% of price after 18 months.

**Reject entirely.** Fundamental and Title warranties need:
- a separate regime;
- a cap of 100% of price;
- a claims period of at least six years;
- carve-outs from the general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.

### C. Fraud carve-out (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)

Applying limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature" would cover fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. This is a non-negotiable point. No one on the deal team can waive it.

**Insert** a carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct, by the Seller or its officers, employees or advisers. It should apply to all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable under NSW law. The same clauses must also carve out Title/Fundamental claims, specific indemnities and payment obligations.

### D. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)

The Seller relies on two general disclosures:
- **1.1:** everything "contained or referred to" in the entire data room, including DD-002 to DD-012.
- **1.2:** the Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records.

Both are deemed disclosure of the kind our playbook rejects. "Referred to" is especially wide: it captures documents that are not even in the data room.

**Push back:**
- Delete 1.1 and 1.2.
- Disclosure should count only if it is **specific and fair**, made against a particular warranty, with enough detail for the Buyer to assess its nature and scope.
- No deemed disclosure of the data room, public registers or anything discoverable by prudent search.
- No disclosure may qualify Title, capacity, specific indemnities or the fraud carve-out.

**Currency:** the letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**, about six weeks ago. Require an updated disclosure letter and a bring-down at Completion. Any new disclosure should not cure warranties without our agreement.

Clause 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable in principle. It must not be read as diluting a specific disclosure the Seller has made.

### E. Buyer knowledge (8.3)

This is a blanket exclusion for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". It duplicates the general disclosure through a second route, and it imputes adviser knowledge to us.

**Delete.** If any qualifier survives:
- It should be **Seller** knowledge, limited to named individuals (we propose the names), after reasonable enquiry.
- It must never excuse Title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### F. Bluefen consent (Cl 3 / 6.3)

The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied once Bluefen's written consent is delivered. Disclosure Letter item 2 confirms that no final consent has been given and there is no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met. Bluefen is about **AUD 3.6m, or ~30%, of FY26 revenue**, so this is a material customer.

**Push back:**
- Make it a hard condition precedent requiring an **effective** consent under DD-002 clause 11.2, in a form we approve.
- Require **evidence before Completion that each clause 11.3 condition is satisfied**.
- Consent-on-delivery is not enough. A consent that is still subject to unmet conditions may not be effective.
- Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a 30% customer. Upgrade to all reasonable endeavours, and preserve the Buyer's sole right to waive.

### G. Riverlark facility (Cl 2 / 7)

The Seller proposes a release "to be provided following Completion" for about **AUD 3.2m** outstanding. Disclosure Letter item 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is in hand. The facility has change-of-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. On a debt-free basis, this must be cleared from the price.

**Push back.** Require at Completion:
- a **current payout letter** from Riverlark, with a per-diem figure;
- **direct repayment from Completion funds** into Riverlark's account, deducted as Debt;
- **executed, effective security releases**, including PPSR discharges and deeds of release, delivered at Completion.

A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an **irrevocable undertaking** from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's written approval. Neither exists, so do not concede it.

Also confirm whether the Riverlark security extends to the sale shares, for example a share mortgage. This ties into Title (section K).

### H. Employee bonuses (funds flow)

The funds flow does not itemise the **AUD 420,000** DD-005 bonuses. The Seller calls them "a matter for the Seller", but the agreement contains no funding mechanism. In practice the Company, and so the Buyer, would bear them after Completion. This is the silent exclusion our playbook prohibits. The disclosure also does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.

**Push back.** Choose one of two routes:
- add a specific funds-flow line item, treated as Debt or Transaction Expenses, for AUD 420,000 **plus all triggered on-costs** (payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, workers' compensation and similar); or
- require an express Seller funding obligation, backed by a specific indemnity outside the general regime.

Also ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position and the payment mechanics through payroll.

### I. Ironquay IP (Cl 11.1)

The existing indemnity is limited to "the specific Statement of Work 3 payment". DD-004 clause 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but that is not independent verification, and we should not assume it is either paid or unpaid.

**Push back:**
- Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold sufficient rights in, the Ironquay deliverables. That includes third-party and Ironquay claims, re-development or licensing costs, and infringement.
- **Preserve the SOW3 cure**: require verified settlement of any outstanding SOW3 fees and an executed confirmatory assignment, ideally as a Completion deliverable.
- Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and time limits.

### J. DD-006 export/privacy incident (4.6 / Schedule 6)

The Seller says the incident is "not expected to be material". Its own disclosure (item 6) says scope, access and notification duty are unresolved and the investigation is preliminary. The materiality assertion has no evidential basis.

**Push back:**
- Reject the materiality characterisation.
- Require the Seller to preserve all logs and evidence, continue a proper investigation, give regular updates before Completion, and give us access to the findings.
- Seek specific protection, such as an indemnity or a specific warranty, covering losses arising from the incident.

Our position should **not** assume a confirmed breach, harm, an NDB notification duty or any loss figure. We should not put a numeric demand or price deduction on it at this stage.

### K. Title evidence

The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register. That is a document the Seller supplied from its own records. It is not independent proof.

**Require:**
- a current ASIC company extract and search;
- the constitution and any shareholder agreement, to confirm no pre-emption or transfer restrictions;
- original or replacement share certificates;
- board minutes approving the transfer;
- PPSR and other encumbrance searches over the shares;
- evidence of Seller authority and capacity, such as a Seller board resolution.

The title warranty itself stays in the Fundamental regime (section B).

### L. Tax / IP warranties

The Seller "considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above". They are **open**. Do not accept this framing. Keep Tax and IP as separate categories, with no folding into the general cap, basket or 18-month period. We are not proposing unlimited liability. Terms remain to be negotiated.

### M. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)

The Seller calls the three renewals "ordinary-course operating costs". Its own disclosure (item 8) says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and that DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together.

**Approach:** assess before taking a position. Request:
- the contracts;
- commitment and termination terms;
- timing against Completion;
- whether amounts are prepaid or accrued;
- whether renewals were entered outside the ordinary course or in contemplation of the sale.

Do not automatically classify them as Debt or seek a price deduction. Consider an interim-period covenant that restricts further renewals without Buyer consent.

### N. Other disclosures (not playbook points, but worth noting)

- **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The Seller's reading is that only a notification is needed (lease) and that no consent is triggered by a share sale (Mossvale). Have our counsel confirm this against the full clauses, including any change-of-control definitions. If confirmed, add the lease notification as a Completion deliverable.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the process framing.** "[STANDARD]", "FINAL" and "settled at principal level" do not bind us. Everything is open, and no fallback has been authorised by Amelia Frost.
2. **Cap and period:** hold at AUD 6.0m (25%) and 24 months. Do not offer 20% or 18 months without Amelia's written authority.
3. **Thresholds:** AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 basket, first dollar once exceeded.
4. **Delete the 12.3/13 sweeper.** Keep Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant regimes separate.
5. **Fundamentals:** separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
6. **Fraud:** full carve-out from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-negotiable.
7. **Disclosure:** specific and fair disclosure only. Delete 1.1 and 1.2, and require an updated letter and bring-down.
8. **Buyer knowledge:** delete 8.3. Any fallback is named-person Seller knowledge after reasonable enquiry.
9. **Bluefen:** hard condition precedent requiring effective consent plus evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Upgrade from reasonable endeavours.
10. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases at Completion. No post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia's approval.
11. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
12. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure (verified payment and confirmatory assignment), and make no assumption about the AUD 180,000.
13. **DD-006:** reject the "not material" label. Require preservation, investigation and updates, and seek specific protection without assuming a breach or quantum.
14. **Sandbar:** information request and assessment first, with no automatic Debt or price treatment.
15. **Title:** independent ASIC, PPSR, constitution, certificate and authority evidence beyond DD-012.
16. **Tax/IP:** remain open and separate. Reject the "settled under the general regime" assertion.

I can turn this into a marked-up issues list or a cover email to Seller's counsel if helpful.
